messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English set in a small neighborhood diner in the evening. Use selective sensory details such as sound, temperature, light, and food without turning the setting into a lyrical description. Let the physical environment affect the characters' interaction in small ways. Keep the prose contemporary, grounded, and specific.

The diner was warm enough that Jordan took off her jacket as soon as they sat down.

The heater under the booth rattled every few minutes. Somewhere behind the counter, dishes clinked together while the coffee machine hissed.

Alex glanced at the menu. “I know what you're getting.”

Jordan looked up. “You don't.”

“Pancakes.”

“Wrong.”

“Waffles.”

“Also wrong.”

Alex lowered the menu. “Then I've learned something tonight.”

Jordan smiled. “Don't get used to it.”

The server dropped off two glasses of water. One had a thin line of condensation running down the side.

Jordan wiped it with her thumb.

“You're getting fries,” Alex said.

“No.”

“You always get fries.”

“I contain multitudes.”

“You contain potatoes.”

Jordan laughed and looked back at the menu.

Outside, headlights slid across the front windows and disappeared. Each time the door opened, a brief wash of cold air moved through the room.

Alex rubbed her hands together after the third one.

“Cold?” Jordan asked.

“A little.”

Jordan pushed the hot coffee closer to her.

Alex looked at the mug. “That's yours.”

“You weren't using it.”

“I was.”

Jordan nudged it another inch.

Alex wrapped both hands around the mug.

“Thanks.”

“Don't mention it.”

A plate landed on the table at the next booth with a sharp clatter.

Jordan flinched.

Alex noticed. “Long day?”

“Long week.”

“You want to talk about it?”

Jordan looked at the steam rising from the coffee.

“Not with an audience.”

Alex glanced around the nearly full diner.

“Fair.”

The server returned with their food.

Jordan looked at her plate, then at Alex.

“You were right.”

“About what?”

“The fries.”

Alex smiled. “I knew it.”

Jordan stole one from her plate anyway.
